recent_posts.title: Gala supercharges analytics performance with ClickHouse on AWS
recent_posts.summary: Gala, a blockchain-powered gaming platform, migrated from Databricks to ClickHouse Cloud on AWS to handle growing analytics demands. The migration tripled data analytics capacity (from 3 TB to 9 TB), reduced costs by 30%, and cut query times from minutes to sub-second. The platform also enabled broader BI access via Metabase integration and reduced engineering overhead spent on infrastructure maintenance.

recent_posts.title: Agentic analytics starts with query-ready data: the write-side cost of Snowflake vs. ClickHouse
recent_posts.summary: Agentic analytics workloads require continuously fresh, query-ready data, making write-side cost a critical metric. This benchmark compares ClickHouse and Snowflake under sustained 1 million rows/second ingest of the ClickBench dataset (100B–300B rows). Snowflake writes data in arrival order and relies on a separate automatic clustering service to establish sorted locality, costing ~$2,885 per 100B rows (ingest + clustering). ClickHouse sorts data at write time and preserves ordering through background merges on the same provisioned nodes, costing ~$131 per 100B rows — 22× cheaper. Combined with faster query execution (126s vs 176s on 100B rows), ClickHouse delivers 28× better write-side cost-performance. Additionally, ClickHouse's progressive consolidation yields 5–15× better compression than Snowflake on the same dataset, reducing storage costs and downstream query I/O.

recent_posts.title: Introducing Postgres Query Insights in ClickHouse Cloud
recent_posts.summary: ClickHouse has launched Postgres Query Insights in preview for ClickHouse Cloud Managed Postgres. Powered by the open-source pg_stat_ch extension (Apache 2.0), it streams per-statement telemetry from Postgres into ClickHouse and surfaces three views: an overview dashboard (query volume, error rate, cache hit ratio, latency), a slow patterns table sortable by total duration, CPU, error count, and P95, and a per-pattern detail flyout showing percentile latencies, cache vs disk reads, temp spills, parallel worker utilization, and WAL volume. A walkthrough demonstrates diagnosing a p99 latency regression caused by sort spills to disk, leading to index and work_mem fixes. Technically, query normalization happens in Postgres before telemetry leaves the database, ensuring PII/PHI never enters the stream. The extension adds ~3% overhead using a non-blocking ring buffer. Upcoming features include an Open API for AI agents, wait event attribution, EXPLAIN plan capture, index/work_mem recommendations, and regression alerts.

recent_posts.title: How Qonto replaced Grafana Tempo with ClickHouse Cloud for full-retention observability
recent_posts.summary: Qonto, a digital bank serving 600K+ businesses across Europe, migrated its observability stack from Grafana Tempo to ClickHouse Cloud, eliminating sampling constraints and extending query windows from 2-3 hours to two weeks. A key win was compression: 231 TB of high-cardinality span attribute data compressed to 376 GB (99.84% ratio), saving ~$70K/year in S3 costs. The team adopted an 'Observability 2.0' philosophy, replacing the logs/metrics/traces three-pillar model with wide structured events stored in a columnar engine. Data flows from applications, Kubernetes, and GitHub through OpenTelemetry collectors to ClickHouse Cloud via AWS PrivateLink, with Grafana for dashboards. On top of this, Qonto built an AI incident companion using the ClickHouse MCP server, allowing anyone to investigate incidents in plain English. The agent runs SQL queries, surfaces trace IDs, and returns structured root-cause summaries — democratizing incident response beyond the SRE team.

recent_posts.title: Stop guessing in production: Full fidelity tracing at scale with ClickHouse and Odigos
recent_posts.summary: Observability gaps in distributed systems often persist even when telemetry exists, because instrumentation is incomplete, trace context breaks across async boundaries, and data lacks actionable context. Combining ClickStack (a ClickHouse-native observability backend) with Odigos (a zero-code OpenTelemetry instrumentation platform using eBPF) addresses this. Odigos attaches to running workloads without code changes, capturing deep telemetry including Kafka message payloads, database queries, stack traces, HTTP headers, and custom business logic. It also manages the OTel collector pipeline automatically. ClickStack ingests this high-fidelity data at scale and makes it queryable via SQL in real time. The result is end-to-end distributed tracing with full context, deployable on Kubernetes via Helm, that eliminates guesswork during production incidents.

recent_posts.title: Comparing ClickHouse versions with clickhousectl
recent_posts.summary: clickhousectl is a CLI tool that lets you install, run, and manage multiple ClickHouse versions side by side. The post walks through installing clickhousectl, spinning up two local ClickHouse servers (versions 25.12 and 26.3), loading 30 million rows of UK property price data, and benchmarking two recent performance improvements: a 5x speedup for DISTINCT queries over low-cardinality columns (introduced in 26.1), and a new Parquet metadata cache (introduced in 26.3) that cuts repeat S3 query times from ~9 seconds down to ~1-2 seconds. The post also covers how to copy table schemas and data between local servers using the CLI.

recent_posts.title: ClickHouse at Google Cloud Next '26
recent_posts.summary: ClickHouse announced several major product launches and integrations at Google Cloud Next 2026. Key highlights include: ClickHouse Cloud running on Google Axion ARM processors with 30-55% faster query performance and ~60% faster data load times; native integration with Google's Lakehouse Runtime Catalog for querying Iceberg tables directly without ETL; BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud) now generally available on Google Cloud Marketplace; and ClickHouse support in Google Antigravity AI IDE via MCP server. Additionally, GCS ClickPipes now supports unordered mode using Pub/Sub notifications for more reliable large-scale pipelines. Upcoming features include a Pub/Sub Dataflow template, BigQuery CDC for ClickPipes, native Pub/Sub ClickPipes connector, Private Service Connect support, and managed Postgres on GCP.

recent_posts.title: What's New in pg_clickhouse - JSONB Support, SQL value functions, Streaming, and more
recent_posts.summary: pg_clickhouse, the PostgreSQL extension for querying ClickHouse databases, has received several notable updates. Version 0.1.10 added JSONB accessor operator and function pushdown (including ->, ->>, jsonb_extract_path, jsonb_extract_path_text) that translates to ClickHouse sub-column syntax. Version 0.2.0 improved pushdown for SQL date/time value functions like CURRENT_DATE, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, clock_timestamp(), and others, ensuring timezone-aware translation to ClickHouse equivalents. Array function pushdown was also added, mapping Postgres functions like array_cat, array_to_string, and string_to_array to their ClickHouse counterparts. Additionally, HTTP result set streaming was introduced, buffering ~50MB at a time instead of loading entire result sets into memory — reducing peak memory usage from 600MB+ to under 86MB when querying large datasets like NYC taxi data.

recent_posts.title: 永産システム開発がいかにClickHouse Cloudを活用し、POS分析を高速、低コストかつ信頼性の高いものにしたか
recent_posts.summary: Eisan System Development, a Japanese software company, replaced their QlikView-based BI stack with ClickHouse Cloud to power an ID-POS analytics platform for retail clients. The legacy system struggled with growing data volumes (up to 200M records per client annually), unpredictable failures, high memory consumption, and escalating licensing costs. After evaluating PostgreSQL and YugabyteDB without success, they discovered ClickHouse and were impressed by its speed without relying on in-memory processing. The migration improved query reliability (zero failed queries vs. frequent failures in QlikView), reduced infrastructure costs, and enabled better resource utilization. The team is now optimizing CPU/memory ratios, exploring autoscaling and planned scaling strategies, and targeting a future scale of 100 billion records.

recent_posts.title: ClickHouse Cloud on Google Cloud Now Powered by Google Axion Processors: 30–55% Faster Queries, ~15% Fewer Compute Credits
recent_posts.summary: ClickHouse Cloud is migrating its Google Cloud fleet from x86 N2D instances to Google Axion C4A (ARM-based) instances. Benchmarks show 30–55% faster ClickBench queries and ~15% fewer compute credits consumed across production workloads. A cohort of 38 migrated services confirmed the efficiency gains on real, diverse traffic. The migration is transparent to customers — no data movement or query changes required — and ClickHouse Cloud on Google Cloud now holds first place on the ClickBench combined ranking. The rollout is ongoing, with Axion expected to become the standard instance type for the platform.
